page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the E2 family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs, which map to 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled at 2 threads per core. It includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and it does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this instance is positioned in the lower tiers for compute-intensive tasks. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1101.98, and the multi-core score is 1451.88, both falling within the bottom 25% and 10% of tested servers respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only small block cached speeds of 80.53 GB/sec, while large block uncached read and write speeds reach 12.0 GB/sec and 10.51 GB/sec. In application-level benchmarks, the instance achieves 1.33 million operations per second on Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 1.43 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-highmem-2 offers a high memory capacity relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high CPU performance. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent, albeit modest, processing power. This hardware profile is best suited for lightweight database operations, caching layers, basic web serving, and small-scale memory-intensive applications that do not demand intensive floating-point calculations or high-throughput parallel processing.
